headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and write conflicts; Dify→Goose output chaining can also cascade errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write uploaded knowledge-base files and shares state via Dify server datastore, while Goose reads/writes the user filesystem and uses MCP extensions. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Goose consumes Dify-produced files or outputs from the shared workspace. The pathway is not proven by docs, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Goose reads Dify-generated files from a shared workspace
IF Dify outputs are treated as instructions by Goose without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of agent-generated files
Add a provenance header check before Goose parses any Dify output
Use read-only mounts for Dify artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge-base content and conversation logs, and Goose touches source code and files in cwd. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so a shared workspace can expose sensitive content from Dify to Goose outputs or external model providers. Because the pair can overlap on the same files and Dify stores shared state, the leakage risk is material in default self-hosted setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or datastore
IF either agent forwards file contents to its model provider or extension backend
mitigations: Use separate OS users and directories
Restrict Goose to a narrow project subtree
Turn off automatic file upload/import where possible
Redact secrets from shared artifacts before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and audit logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells; Goose also modifies git state and uses filesystem-based shared state, while Dify can run server-side code and write uploaded files. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt files or git history without locking. This is a direct overlap in mutable resources, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF either agent writes without an external lock or transaction boundary
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Pause one agent during the other's write phase
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Add a file-locking wrapper around shared paths
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit agent/workflow outputs, and Goose is a coding agent with shell and MCP tools. If Goose consumes Dify output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Dify result can trigger downstream actions. The docs do not prove a default trust chain, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Goose uses Dify output as direct input to tool calls
IF no verification step checks Dify-produced facts before action
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require structured output with schema validation
Compare Dify claims against source files before acting
Limit Goose to read-only mode for Dify-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while Goose touches source code and files in cwd. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared workspace, differing retention or residency controls could apply across the two systems. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits the documented policy gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF Goose processes the same regulated data under a different retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Document retention and deletion procedures for both agents
Use separate storage buckets for sensitive content
Review vendor DPA and residency terms before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion controls
